Subject: Proposed DPA language — breach notification & incident cooperation

Team / Michael —

Below is proposed redline language intended as a compromise between BlueHarbor's 24-hour request and Redwood's operational needs. Please review and advise.

1) Initial notification: "Processor shall notify Controller of a confirmed or reasonably suspected personal data security incident affecting Controller's data without undue delay and, in any event, within forty-eight (48) hours of Processor's discovery of the incident. Initial notification will contain a high-level description of the nature of the incident, categories of affected data, estimated scope, and contact point for further coordination."

2) Follow-up reporting: "Processor shall provide a detailed incident report within five (5) business days of the initial notification, which will include cause analysis to the extent available, immediate containment/mitigation measures taken, and proposed remediation steps. A final report, including root cause analysis and long-term remediation plan, will be delivered no later than thirty (30) days after the initial notification, subject to reasonable extensions for ongoing criminal or regulatory investigations."

3) Incident cooperation: "Processor will cooperate with Controller's reasonable requests, including preserving forensic artifacts, providing IOCs, providing technical logs (subject to redaction of other customers' data where applicable), and supporting Controller's regulatory notifications. Costs associated with Controller-initiated on-site forensics shall be pre-approved and invoiced to Controller unless Processor's negligence is established."

4) Subprocessors and notification: "Processor will provide Controller with a list of current subprocessors prior to execution and will provide at least thirty (30) calendar days' written notice for any additions. Controller shall have the right to object to a new subprocessor within fifteen (15) calendar days, which obligation shall be exercised reasonably and in good faith. If Controller objects and the parties cannot agree on mitigation within fifteen (15) calendar days, either party may terminate the affected Services for that Controller without additional liability."

Rationale: 48 hours balances the controller's desire for rapid awareness with our need to triage false positives and gather minimally verified facts. Five business days for initial detail gives security teams time to collect material facts; 30 days for the full report is consistent with industry practice for meaningful RCA.

We can narrow "without undue delay" to remove ambiguity and keep the 48-hour backstop if BlueHarbor insists.

If BlueHarbor accepts, we can convert to clean DPA, build the DocuSign envelope (signing order: BlueHarbor CFO -> BlueHarbor Legal -> Redwood Legal -> Redwood Sales), and target execution within 72 hours.

-Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
